rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sequential read of all 14 chunks: every pronoun/demonstrative resolves within-chunk or against an earlier-named term of the same file (e.g. chunk 8 line 79 'The other kind' resolves against chunk 7's 'two kinds' split; chunk 10 line 93 'a subagent doing your noisy reading' resolves against chunk 4's 'Subagent as a firewall'). 'Module 3' (chunk 4 line 49) is itself an unambiguous, fully-named referent under this rule — it does not fail resolution. (Its problem is temporal/positional validity across the file's documented multiple entry points, which is a rule 2 concern, filed there.) No never-named, no vague-with-history, no stranded-by-rechunk referent found otherwise.

Chunk 4 "The craft: spend and route wisely", line 49: "You'll meet it properly, mechanism and trade-off both, in Module 3." This replaced "...later in the training." in commit 1c9215cd (2026-08-20), which lands AFTER this file's slides class was last stamped (pin 3902c345, 2026-08-19, per the current Quality line) — this exact sentence has never been slides-judged before now. The maintainer Placement block (line ~135) documents THREE entry points for this one file: M2 close (final slide of `how-instructions-grow.md`), M3 module close (`earn-the-trust.md`), and M4 prework (`run-the-first-experiment.md`). Module order per `site/layouts/curriculum.js` TRAININGS['agentic-engineering-101'].modules: M1 getting-going, M2 plan-mode-done-right, M3 earn-the-trust, M4 run-the-first-experiment. The sentence is future tense ('You'll meet') and is only true from the M2-close entry point. At the M3-close entry point it describes the very module the reader is finishing as still forthcoming; at the M4-prework entry point it is flatly false — that reader has already completed M3, where subagents are in fact already used (`earn-the-trust.md` lines 23-24: 'Invoke curated ... skills ... each as a subagent, fresh context' and 'Split jobs between subagent and main thread', with the mechanism/trade-off detail linked from the module's own Prework at line 18). Rule 11 states the same principle directly: 'Cross-file phase refs → maintainer block only, file-qualified (body cross-file positional callbacks already banned per §2)' — a body sentence identifying content by its ordinal position in the cross-file module arc is exactly what §2 bans, whether phrased relatively ('the opening lecture') or by absolute ordinal ('Module 3'); the harm is the same, a claim whose truth depends on where in the arc the reader currently sits, and this file is placed at three different arc positions by design. Harm: a reader who arrives via the M4-prework placement — a position the maintainer block itself specifies — is told a primitive they already used two module-closes ago is still to come, which reads as an authoring error or makes them doubt whether what M3 gave them was 'the real' treatment. That is a trust cost on a page whose whole second half ('The folklore') is built to earn the reader's trust in its own accuracy.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name the primitive by its claim/mechanism rather than a module ordinal (e.g. drop the module reference and let 'You'll meet it properly, mechanism and trade-off both' stand alone, or name what the trade-off actually is in one clause) so the sentence holds at all three documented entry points; if a module pointer is wanted for the M2-close reading specifically, it belongs in the maintainer block per rule 11, not the shared body all three entry points render.

Every chunk carries a self-standing claim even read cold: e.g. chunk 9 'Drivers of inefficient context: fanning out is its own bill' (lines 87-89), the shortest chunk in the file at 3 sentences, still states its own thesis (fan-out is a real but contested cost, treat as a ceiling not a default) rather than leaning on a wait-state or one context-dependent bullet. Checked all 13 `##` headers against their own chunk body under the sequential read; each is a literally true summary (e.g. line 87 'fanning out is its own bill' matches its body's fan-out-cost claim; line 61 'The folklore: numbers that don't survive a second look' matches the two debunked round-number claims that follow). Closest call: line 45 'The craft: spend and route wisely' against its third bullet, 'Keep what you carry lean' (line 53) — reads more like restraint on input than active spend/routing, but the chunk's own framing sentence ('The rest are about what you do with the work once it's in front of you') covers it loosely enough that the header still holds as a fair summary.

Grepped body (lines 1-120) for 'Not X. Not Y.' constructions (zero), anaphora/epistrophe triples (zero), self-grading superlatives (zero matches of the training/exercise praising its own usefulness), number+own-retraction pairs (zero — all figures, e.g. the $10/$2 comparison at line 33 and the 23-54% at line 9, are stated once with sourcing, never hedged-then-undercut), abstraction-noun stacks (zero; 'Absorption bottleneck' only appears in the backing block below the maintainer cut, out of body scope), and empty-leg verb triplets (zero). Closest call: line 41 'the cheapest quality upgrade there is, and the most skipped' is superlative-shaped but grades the /clear habit, not this page/training/exercise, so it does not match `check_writing.md §13`'s value-prop-leak target (a claim about the training's own usefulness).
